content:
Apple has rolled out the first developer beta of iOS 27.2 for iPhone. The update comes just after iOS 27 was officially released to all users on Monday. The update also skips iOS 27.1, which Apple had been positioning as an update targeting iPhone Duo.

iOS 27.2 beta 1 arrives before iOS 27.1 beta

This beta release comes just after iOS 27 officially launched on September 14. The new version is a sizable update, coming in at 22GB.

Apple has previously detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK will let developers take full advantage of the iPhone Duo display. You can see here how apps will look differently on iPhone Duo depending on which iOS version they target.

But this release of iOS 27.2 developer beta 1 currently skips over iOS 27.1.

Apple appears to be holding back iPhone Duo-specific code until closer to its new hardware launch in October. However, developers still need to prepare for the new device. Apple says the related tools are expected to be ready before the end of September.

Apple has also teased other changes coming to all iPhones next month, including a redesigned Apple Health app and expanded Siri AI support.

Apple confirmed this week: "Siri AI begins rolling out in English, offering a more powerful, conversational assistant experience with personalized context understanding, broad world knowledge, on-screen content awareness, and deeper system-wide app actions; French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish support will arrive in October."

This may give us an idea of when to expect the official release.

Once we've actually run this first beta, we'll have a much clearer picture of what Apple has included.

We'll be putting together a detailed rundown of the new features and other changes as we explore this new beta. Stay tuned for our continued coverage of the iOS 27.2 beta.
